clue.text: Cathedral city, central accordingly to head of diocese

indicators.note: central asks for only the inner part of the word, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: accordingly means therefore

indicators.note: head of asks for the first letter of the word diocese

explanation.surface: A guidebook note on a cathedral city sitting at the centre of a bishop's diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: THEREFORE loses its first and last letters to give HEREFOR, then D from diocese ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford is an English city whose cathedral holds the Mappa Mundi.

clue.text: Raising family in mostly elevated surroundings

indicators.note: in places the family word inside the shortened word, the 'surroundings'
mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: elevated means high
family means kin

explanation.surface: A family brought up somewhere lofty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' backs up 'in': the elevated word, cut short by 'mostly', surrounds the family.
explanation.definitionFit: To hike prices is to raise them, so hiking can stand for raising.

clue.text: Take part in race — a bad-tempered encounter

parts.note: to take part in a race is to run
bad-tempered means cross

explanation.surface: An athlete in a race has an angry clash with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To run across someone is to meet them by chance, an encounter.

clue.text: Drunken sot collected by man in white coat

indicators.note: collected by means held inside the man's name

parts.note: Fred is a man's name

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk is picked up by a doctor or orderly in a white coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in white coat' sounds like a doctor's coat, but it is the definition: covered in frost or icing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frosted has a coating of white frost or icing.

clue.text: Eager male chasing rodent

indicators.note: chasing puts the male word behind the rodent, running after it

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A keen man running after a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an old word for early or eager, prompt in action.

clue.text: Gnome turned and escorted to departure

parts.note: a gnome is a pithy saying, a saw
milk that has turned has gone off

explanation.surface: A garden gnome is rotated and walked to the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' here is a maxim, not a garden ornament; 'turned' means soured.
explanation.definitionFit: To see someone off is to accompany them as they leave, so saw off means escorted to departure.

clue.text: Seafood sustaining sailor on solo voyage?

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
someone on a solo voyage is alone

explanation.surface: Shellfish keeping a lone yachtsman fed.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail, a prized shellfish.

clue.text: Subject moves head to centre of vision

indicators.note: says the first letter of the word is shifted into the middle

parts.note: a subject is a topic

explanation.surface: Someone shifts their head into the middle of the view.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of TOPIC moves to the middle: O-P-T-I-C.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective meaning relating to the eye or sight.

clue.text: Minor champ gets to run around a little

indicators.note: around places the run word about the little word

parts.note: to run away is to flee
a little means a bit

explanation.surface: A small-time winner gets to jog around for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' is not a winner but a chew, a bite; A BIT goes inside FLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A champ is a bite, so a minor one is a small insect's nip, a trivial injury.

clue.text: Put plan into action

indicators.note: into puts the plan word inside the action word

parts.note: an action is a deed
a plan or scheme is a ploy

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry out a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is the definition, past tense, not part of 'put into'.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops deployed have been put in position, so deployed means placed.

clue.text: Many's the time man is captured by chess pieces in game

indicators.note: captured by means held between the chess pieces

parts.note: the king is a chess piece
the castle, or rook, is a chess piece
many's the time means often, oft
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A player's man is often taken by chess pieces during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a chess capture; really both pieces stand round the time and the man.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's game where one player holds a mound against all challengers.

clue.text: Formal wear imposing restriction on kiss

indicators.note: on puts the restriction after the kiss in an across answer

parts.note: to neck is to kiss
a tie is a restriction or constraint

explanation.surface: Dressing up for an occasion puts a stop to romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is worn with formal clothes such as a suit.

clue.text: Young Daniel subdued?

parts.note: Daniel in the lions' den tamed the beasts; a youngster of that kind is the cryptic reading

explanation.definitionFit: A young lion, the kind of creature the biblical Daniel overcame in the den.

clue.text: Wit acts on rumour

indicators.note: on puts the acts word after the rumour word

parts.note: word means news or rumour, as in 'word has it'
a play is made of acts

explanation.surface: A comedian performs on the strength of gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordplay is verbal wit, such as punning.

clue.text: Opera makes room for experimenting with love motif that's timeless

parts.note: a lab is a room for experiments
love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: timeless means the time letter T is removed

parts.note: a motif is a theme

explanation.surface: An opera leaves space for trying out an eternal love theme.
explanation.walkthrough: THEME without T gives HEME.
explanation.definitionFit: La Bohème is Puccini's opera of Parisian artists.

clue.text: Wader rescued from water gently returned

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
rescued from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A heron-like bird is pulled out of the water and gently put back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Wader rescued' as the definition, but 'rescued from' is the hidden-word signal and the definition is 'Wader' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: Runs fail-safe manoeuvres in plant

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests the letters are moved into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Military exercises that cannot go wrong held at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is the definition; 'manoeuvres' gives AFFLESIA from fail-safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafflesia is a parasitic plant with the world's largest single flower.

clue.text: Belt with river's kept in mind for homeowner

indicators.note: kept in means held inside the belt word

parts.note: to belt is to hit
the Ouse is an English river; river's gives Ouse's, with the S

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a strap and a river in their thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire; 'mind' is the verb, look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To house-sit is to look after a home while its owner is away.

clue.text: Haven offering nothing in the circumstances

parts.note: nothing is zero, O
as is means in the present state, in the circumstances

explanation.surface: A refuge that gives nothing given how things are.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a refuge, a place of calm, like a watering spot in a desert.

clue.text: Philosopher visiting Australia in spring

indicators.note: in places the visiting word and Australia inside the spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
visiting means in, as in 'in town'
Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: A thinker on a trip to Australia in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' is not the season but a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a seventeenth-century Dutch philosopher.

clue.text: Poor start by lad confused at first

indicators.note: at first says the jumbled letters come before the start word
confused suggests the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the off is the start of a race

explanation.surface: A boy muddled from the outset makes a bad beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' looks like part of the surface, but it is the off of a race; 'confused' gives BADLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Badly off means short of money, poor.

clue.text: Snacks upset Roy's gut

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters are overturned and rearranged

explanation.surface: Snacks that disagree with Roy's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots of yogurt are a common light snack.

clue.text: Actively tinker, poking nose in

indicators.note: in puts the nosy word inside the tinker

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
to pry is to poke one's nose into things

explanation.surface: A busy tinkerer sticks his nose into things.
explanation.walkthrough: Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Spryly means in a lively, active way.

clue.text: Mean to have job in Billingsgate — only one left

indicators.note: only one left says one of the two Ls (left) is dropped

parts.note: Billingsgate is London's fish market, where the job is to sell fish
the other half of the job: the goods sold at Billingsgate are fish

explanation.surface: A stingy fishmonger at a London market keeps just one fish back.
explanation.walkthrough: SELL FISH loses one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean, selfish person thinks only of themselves.

clue.text: Composer cut singer short: sorry for interrupting!

indicators.note: cut says the shortened singer is split open by the apology
short says the bird's name stops one letter early

parts.note: the lark is a songbird
eh? is the interjection of someone breaking in, like 'sorry?'

explanation.surface: A musician breaks off a singer mid-note and apologises for butting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' reads with 'short', but here it is the container signal: the apology cuts into the trimmed songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar composed the operetta The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Drink gives one urge to go mad

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
to flip is to go mad

explanation.surface: A drink makes someone want to go crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg flip is a drink of beaten egg with milk or alcohol.

clue.text: Wooden frame found in Leisure Centre of old

parts.note: ease is leisure

indicators.note: centre of asks for the middle letter

explanation.surface: An old wooden frame turns up in a sports hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leisure Centre' reads as a sports hall but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a wooden stand for a painter's canvas.

clue.text: Learner in chemistry's so-so — resolves to like teacher

indicators.note: resolves means it is broken up and resolved into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner

explanation.surface: A student's chemistry is mediocre, so they decide to act like a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: L and CHEMISTRY'S SO-SO rearrange together.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolmistressy describes the prim manner of a teacher.

clue.text: Horse brings slate to desert from East

indicators.note: from East says the desert word is read right to left

parts.note: to rat is to desert
to slate or pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A horseman takes roofing slate to the desert from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: RAT reversed is TAR; 'slate' means criticise, PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarpan is an extinct wild horse of Europe.

clue.text: A sucker ultimately taken in by polished set of explanations

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside the polished word

parts.note: glossy means polished

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the last letter of sucker

explanation.surface: A gullible person is fooled by slick explanations.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R go into GLOSSY.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of difficult words with their meanings.
